item.title: Sanctioned 22-Year-Old Tanker Makes Rare Late-Season Arctic Voyage
item.dc:creator: Malte Humpert
item.description: A 22-year-old product tanker sanctioned by the European Union is making an unusual late-season voyage along Russia's Northern Sea Route, highlighting the growing use of older, lower-specification vessels to move petroleum products through the Arctic.

item.title: South Korea Denies Ukrainian Report That It Eased Russia’s Fuel Crisis
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: South Korea's presidential office on Wednesday dismissed a Ukrainian report that Russia has imported petroleum products from South Korean ports, calling the accusation inappropriate.

item.title: Port of Savannah Sets September Container Record as Imports Rise
item.dc:creator: Mike Schuler
item.description: The Port of Savannah handled a record 504,015 twenty-foot equivalent units in September, up 3.7% from a year earlier as strong imports and a later-than-usual peak season boosted volumes.

item.title: Trafigura Buys Seven Oil Tankers From SFL as Shipping Costs Rise
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Trafigura Group bought seven oil tankers from New York-listed SFL Corp., in the latest example of how trading houses and state energy companies are acquiring vessels to ship crude and products.

item.title: New Maryland Defense Shipyard Gets $6.6 Billion Commitment and Trump Visit
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Defense tech firm Anduril unveiled plans on Tuesday for a $3.7 billion shipyard in Maryland that is expected to generate 3,100 jobs, in a ceremony attended by President Donald Trump.

item.title: Ships Take Long Way Around as Drought Snarls Panama Canal
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Maritime traffic through the Strait of Magellan jumped more than 70% both in August and September from year-ago levels as ships diverted from the drought-stricken Panama Canal, Chilean Navy data requested by Bloomberg show.

item.title: Attacks on Tankers in Hormuz Hit Highest of Any Week Since Start of Iran War, Sources Say
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: Attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest last week of any week since the Iran war began, according to maritime security sources tracking incidents, amid a bigger export push by Gulf producers.

item.title: China Completes First Season of Regular Arctic Container Service
item.dc:creator: Malte Humpert
item.description: China has completed the first season of regular weekly container shipping between China and Europe via the Northern Sea Route, with the operator completing all eight sailings planned for 2026 before ending departures slightly earlier than scheduled because of Arctic ice forecasts.

item.title: Qatar Brings Empty LNG Ships Into Gulf in Potential Export Boost
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.description: Qatar has amassed a fleet of empty liquefied natural gas tankers in the Persian Gulf, a sign that one of the world’s biggest exporters of the fuel may be preparing to boost shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
